judged_text: The inline contract for the sync endpoint — "The response should only contain the access token and expiry date" — contradicts what this diff's consumers actually require: Lark's handleLarkError demands the Lark envelope {code, msg, data}, Google/Hubspot/Zoho need provider-native objects (and crash per the shape findings), and Zoom/O365/Webex/Teams each parse their app-native token bodies. A parent-app implementer who builds to the documented contract gets an endpoint that works for none of the apps: lark-calendar sync permanently fails in handleLarkError on the bare {access_token} body, with an error that gives no hint the response shape is the problem; the real per-app contract exists only in each consumer's error handler.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens()` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, calls `fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns that response (a Fetch `Response`) while its call sites continue to expect provider-native/token-library-native shapes. Examples in the diff: Google Calendar expects `res?.data` after `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` (but Fetch `Response` has no `.data`), and Lark passes the returned value to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)`, which (by its type usage) expects a Lark API response that can be parsed as `RefreshTokenResp`, not a generic `{access_token, expiry}` contract. Similarly, Hubspot/Zoho callers type the return as token objects/axios responses, but in sync mode they would receive a Fetch `Response`. This makes the inline contract comment in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` (“response should only contain the access token and expiry date”) incompatible with how the diff’s consumers actually handle the returned value, causing broken runtime behavior when the sync feature is enabled.
